summary: Néma Airport (EMN/GQNI) is a small regional airport serving the remote city of Néma in southeastern Mauritania, capital of the Hodh Ech Chargui region near the Mali border. The facility primarily supports domestic connectivity and humanitarian operations in one of the country's most isolated areas. It features a single unpaved or rudimentary runway suited to the demands of the Sahelian environment.
faqs:
Q: What is Néma Airport primarily used for?
A: It serves domestic flights and humanitarian missions, connecting this remote southeastern Mauritanian region to the capital Nouakchott and other hubs.

Q: Are there international flights from Néma Airport?
A: No, the airport handles only domestic operations with limited scheduled service.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small regional facility, amenities are minimal, typically consisting of a basic terminal and parking area.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Néma?
A: The cooler dry season from November to March is generally most comfortable, as extreme summer heat in the Sahel can affect schedules.
transport_tips: Taxis and shared 4x4 vehicles are typically the main way to reach the airport from central Néma, which is only a short drive away. Road conditions in the region can be rough, especially during the rainy season, so allow extra travel time. Travelers should arrange ground transport in advance, as options near the airport are limited.
local_tip: Carry sufficient cash in Mauritanian ouguiya, as ATMs are scarce in Néma and the airport has no reliable payment infrastructure for taxis or services.
